---
title: "check-heading-siblings.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags a heading a pull request adds
to a group of too many sibling headings.
Sibling headings are headings of the same level under the same parent heading;
the top-level headings of a page are siblings under the page.
The lab's guideline (Ezra, 2026-11-02) is to aim for at most about five
and to split or group past seven,
so a reader scanning the headings can hold them all in mind.
Miller's
["magical number seven"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Magical_Number_Seven,_Plus_or_Minus_Two)
and Cowan's later
[estimate of about four chunks](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/behavioral-and-brain-sciences/article/magical-number-4-in-shortterm-memory-a-reconsideration-of-mental-storage-capacity/44023F1147D4A1D44BDC0AD226838496)
motivate the guideline; both concern memory,
and a reader can rescan a table of contents,
so the check fires at the seven where the guideline says to act, not at five.

## What it measures

The check counts headings on the *expanded* page,
the page's own text with each `{{< include >}}` shortcode
replaced by the file it names,
since a chapter's headings are often split across subfiles.
Headings inside fenced code blocks and HTML comments do not count.
A heading's parent is the nearest earlier heading of a lower level.

## Decision record

The threshold of 7 was chosen on 2026-11-02
to match the guideline's "split or group past seven".
On first measurement of the source trees,
the check finds crowded groups in lds, sds and psw and none in pds.
To reproduce, run the check with `whole-tree: true` in a checkout of each repository.
Change the default in `check-heading-siblings.py`, `action.yml`
and the reusable workflow together.

## What it flags

A group of more than `max` siblings,
when the pull request adds one of its headings to the page or to a file it includes.
The finding sits on the first added heading of the group.
A group the diff did not add a heading to is not reflagged, so nothing is swept.
`<!-- check-heading-siblings: allow -->`
anywhere in the page's own file exempts it.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to measure every tracked page in full.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default    | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd'`  | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`       | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. |
| `max`          | string  | `'7'`      | Largest number of sibling headings under one parent. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `false`    | Fail the workflow when a touched group is over the limit. The default gives warning annotations only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`    | Measure every tracked page in full instead of only touched pages. |

## Usage

```yaml
jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-heading-siblings.yml@v3
```

Copy [`examples/check-heading-siblings.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-heading-siblings.yml).
